notes: Méribel side, the Tour route of 2020/2023/2025 (Brides-les-Bains – Les Allues – Méribel – voie verte). Route through Méribel per the resort's Tour road-closure notice: D90 Route de Méribel from Mussillon to Rue des Jeux Olympiques / Rue Albert Gacon, Rue des Jeux Olympiques, Rue des Glaciers, Route de l'Altiport from the school (Route de l'Agentila junction) up to the Route du Belvédère, Route du Belvédère to the entrance of the voie verte, then the car-free cycle road (Overture: cycleway, then 'Route du Col de la Loze' unclassified) to the col (2304 m, where the Méribel and Courchevel branches meet; Wikipedia's rounded coordinate 45.4050, 6.6019 lies ~300 m before it on the same road). The waypoints name 'cycleway' as road so the pipeline unlocks the cycle path. km 0: the app's 10.5 km profile only fits a foot 10.5 km before the col on this route, i.e. on the D90 at Mussillon at the north entrance of Méribel (GLO-30 ~1410 m, app 1435 m): from there the routed km 4-10.5 elevations match the app profile within ~10 m and the voie verte begins at ~3.35 km (app landmark 'Beginn des Radwegs' 3.4 km). Climbfinder's 'from Méribel' version starts 0.3 km later in the centre (10.2 km, 870 m). Routed on Overture 10.42 km; km values scaled by 10.5/10.422. The Méribel Altiport itself (~45.408, 6.581) is not on the route; the voie verte turns away below it.
sources: Overture Maps 2026-10-21.0 transportation segments (Route de Méribel, Rue des Jeux Olympiques, Rue des Glaciers, Route de l'Altiport, Route du Belvédère, Route du Col de la Loze cycleway) and divisions (Mussillon, Meribel-les-Allues)
